preconditions.description: The number of points n is between 1 and 100 inclusive.
The number of segments m is between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= xi <= 100 for xi in x)
preconditions.description: Each point coordinate xi is between 0 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= li <= ri <= 100 for li, ri in segments)
preconditions.description: Each segment [li, ri] has borders such that 0 ≤ li ≤ ri ≤ 100.
The number of point coordinates matches the given n.
The number of segments matches the given m.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or (len(return_value.split()) == n and all(c in '01' for c in return_value.split()))
postconditions.description: The output is either '-1' or a string of n binary digits (0 or 1).

postconditions.expression: return_value != '-1' or not all(abs(sum(1 for xi in x if li <= xi <= ri and c == '0') - sum(1 for xi in x if li <= xi <= ri and c == '1')) <= 1 for li, ri in segments for c in ['0', '1'])
postconditions.description: If the output is not '-1', then there exists a valid coloring of points that satisfies the segment condition.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all(abs(sum(1 for xi in x if li <= xi <= ri and return_value.split()[x.index(xi)] == '0') - sum(1 for xi in x if li <= xi <= ri and return_value.split()[x.index(xi)] == '1')) <= 1 for li, ri in segments)
postconditions.description: If the output is not '-1', then the coloring of points satisfies the segment condition for all segments.
